Test counts on the Pi: test_board.py 228 PASS + 1 SKIP; test_kismet_v3.py 299 PASS (297 + 1 SKIP without openssl); remote_e2e.sh 78 PASS; kismet_e2e.sh 42 PASS + 1 SKIP; all ALL OK
Python versions: 3.9.25 (with websocket-client 1.8.0), 3.10.21, 3.11.16 and 3.12.14: both test files ALL OK and a real capture each; 3.13.5 venv: everything

problems.summary: A second remote helper with the same definition (same UUID) knocks out a running one. Kismet closes the running connection and the newcomer's; if the two keep retrying, they keep kicking each other off.
problems.evidence: In p5, while the holder was capturing, a third Python helper with --source esp32c5-ttyACM0 connected. Kismet logged: "ERROR: Incoming remote connection for source 'E5C50001-...0540' matches existing source 'esp32c5-ttyACM0', which is still running. The running instance will be closed; make sure that multiple remote captures are not running", then 'Error reconnecting remote source ... - source closed'. The holder stopped at 488 packets. A retrying Kismet local source then took the board and switched it to BLE. In p6 a leftover helper caused the same repeated drops ('The running instance will be closed' 3 times in 40 s).
problems.suggested_fix: Document it in Multiple-Boards, Remote-Capture and Troubleshooting: never run two helpers with the same definition, e.g. a service plus a manual run. Optionally have the helper back off, or say so clearly, when Kismet closes its connection right after the NEWSOURCE.

problems.summary: Kismet keeps and merges the options of a remote source it has seen before. A reconnect under the same UUID with a different definition keeps the old channel_hop=false, channel= and channels= options.
problems.evidence: p4b, one Kismet run: a 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36,channel_hop=false,name=lock36' session, then plain 'esp32c5-ttyACM0'. REST definition 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36,channel_hop=false,name=lock36', hopping 0, 1 CHANNELS write. The OPENREQ carried the merged definition (helper log: 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36,channel_hop=false,name=lock36: opening /dev/ttyACM0'). The C remote helper got the same result. Only an explicit ':channel_hop=true' unlocked it. The same merge made p4's 'hopping' test source actually locked, and a later channels list gave hop_rate 0 with hopping=1.
problems.suggested_fix: Document it: within one Kismet run, a remote source that reconnects under a known UUID keeps its earlier options, and to unlock you write channel_hop=true or restart Kismet. Correct any claim that the new definition replaces the old one.

problems.summary: close_source.cmd (or closing a source in the web UI) does not keep a Python remote source closed. The helper logs 'Connection to remote host was lost.', not the Troubleshooting row 'Kismet shut the source down: <reason>'.
problems.evidence: p8: close_source.cmd gave Kismet 'Closing source 'esp32c5-ttyACM0''. The helper logged 'connection ended: Connection to remote host was lost.', reconnected 5 s later and was capturing again (running=1 at t+4 s). A following open_source.cmd returned HTTP 500 'ERROR: source already running'.
problems.suggested_fix: Fix the table row at line 460. Say in Source-Definitions and Remote-Capture that closing a remote source in Kismet only lasts until the helper reconnects; stop the helper to keep it closed.

problems.summary: The Troubleshooting and Remote-Capture 401 texts do not match the final code, and 'a key without the datasource role' is not quite right: an admin-role key also works.
problems.evidence: Final code hint: '(check the login -- --user/--password or KISMET_CAP_USER/KISMET_CAP_PASSWORD -- or the API key -- --apikey or KISMET_CAP_APIKEY; the key needs the datasource role)'. The wiki (Troubleshooting 364, Remote-Capture 262, Install-on-Windows 378, Guide-Windows-Boards 238) still quotes '(check --user/--password, or --apikey: the key needs the datasource role)'. The real details are 'Handshake status 401 Unauthorized -+-+- {headers} -+-+- <html>...'. p20: datasource and admin keys were accepted on the websocket; readonly, logon and scanreport keys got 401.
problems.suggested_fix: Quote the new hint text, and say the key needs the datasource (or admin) role.

problems.summary: A password with '&' cannot be used for the Python helper's websocket login. The C helper also fails with a space or '%41'. The login and API key go in the URL query, where proxy access logs record them.
problems.evidence: p15: 'ab&cd12' gave 401 for Python with --password and with KISMET_CAP_PASSWORD. 'ab cd12' and 'ab%41cd12' worked for Python and failed for C ('FATAL: Datasource could not connect websocket client'). API keys always worked. p14: the TLS proxy logged 'GET /datasource/remote/remotesource.ws?KISMET=<key>'.
problems.suggested_fix: State the character limits per helper, recommend API keys, and warn that reverse proxies log the query string.

problems.summary: minicom (no flock and no TIOCEXCL) cannot keep the helpers off a board, and screen leaves a detached SCREEN process holding the port.
problems.evidence: p21c: with minicom holding ttyACM2, the Python helper opened it and logged 'device reports readiness to read but returned no data (device disconnected or multiple access on port?)'. The C local btle source opened it and rebooted the board into BLE (minicom saw 4 boot texts). p21b: after its client was killed, the SCREEN backend (pid 382169) kept /dev/ttyACM2 exclusive, and every later open got EBUSY until it was killed.
problems.suggested_fix: Say that picocom and miniterm take the flock, and screen takes TIOCEXCL, but minicom does neither. Close minicom before starting a source, and check for a detached screen ('screen -ls') when a port is busy.

problems.summary: Without channel_hop=false, channel= is not honoured at the start by the Python helper: the first START already carries the hop list's channel.
problems.evidence: p4c, fresh Kismet, 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36': strace shows 'CHANNELS 1', '5', '9', '13', then 'CHANNELS 13\nDWELL 250\nSTART ...'. REST reports channel '36'. Kismet's CONFIGREQ hop list arrives during the 0.8 s MODE settle.
problems.suggested_fix: Either delay the hopper's first tune until after the first START, or document that channel= without channel_hop=false only sets the REST start value.

problems.summary: BTLE channel=38 and set_channel 38 are accepted, but REST then reports channel '38' while the board scans 37/38/39. With channel=38 Kismet also adds 38 to the hop list.
problems.evidence: p4: 'esp32c5btle-ttyACM3:channel=38' gave channel '37', hop_channels [37,38]. After set_channel {"channel":"38"}: channel '38', hopping 0. The serial writes were only 'MODE BLE' and 'CHANNELS 37...'.
problems.suggested_fix: Report 37 back in the CONFIGREPORT for any BTLE channel (as the start channel does), or document it in Bluetooth-LE-Capture and Channel-Control.

problems.summary: Kismet counts a repeated TXTEST 200 as duplicates, and kismetdb logs 802.15.4 packets with frequency 0.
problems.evidence: p3 kismetdb: the second batch of 200 identical frames (same seq 0-199) was logged with phyname 'Unknown' and MACs 00:00:00:00:00:00. The device counts stayed at 200 while num_packets reached 400. Every 802.15.4 packet has frequency 0.0, though the devices show 2450000 kHz and signal 6.
problems.suggested_fix: Note that device counts rise by 200 only for the first TXTEST in a Kismet session. The frequency=0 in kismetdb comes from the Python helper's signal block, and the C helper was not compared.

problems.summary: The wiki's test counts are out of date.
problems.evidence: p16: test_board.py 228 PASS + 1 SKIP (wiki: 218). kismet_e2e.sh 42 PASS + 1 SKIP (wiki: 46). test_kismet_v3.py 299 PASS. The SKIP lines: 'SKIP an open refused with EBUSY (needs root and capsh, to try it without CAP_SYS_ADMIN)' and 'SKIP wss to localhost with a certificate for localhost (no openssl to make one)'.
problems.suggested_fix: Update the counts, and add the EBUSY SKIP line to the SKIP table.

problems.summary: The Pi's repo copy (~/esp32c5-kismet-wifi-interface) is older than the Windows repo. The tests ran on the newer code copied to ~/e2e/py/src.
problems.evidence: sha256 differs for all four esp32c5_kismet files (Pi remote.py aba8a347... vs Windows 35c5ffae...). The differences are docstrings, the --help epilog and the 401 hint text; the code paths are the same.
problems.suggested_fix: Sync the Pi copy before quoting its message texts.

skeptic.summary:
I checked every C and Python claim against the saved files in scratchpad\hw2 and on the Pi, read-only. I opened no port and started nothing. The Pi is clean now: no kismet, helper, python or strace process, no flock on ttyACM0-3, no open fds and no extra user units. I could not confirm Wi-Fi mode without opening a port, which I was not allowed to do. The installed C helper matches the Windows repo apart from comments. The Pi repo's remote.py differs from the tested copy only in help and hint text, as the Python run said.

Most headline verdicts hold. 1d, 5a, 5b, 5c, 7a, 7b, 8a, 8c, the 15 s check, Python checks 4 and 8, and Python findings 1, 4 and 5 are backed by the files.

Problems the runs missed:
(1) The Python p5 'holder' helper (pid 327923) was never stopped. It ran from 09:45:38 to 09:53:43 and reconnected into p6's Kismet with the same login and UUID. It captured ttyACM0 three times, which explains p6's 'already in use' refusals and the 'Incoming remote connection ... still running' lines (hw2\py\results\py\p5.hold.log).
(2) n8r.out shows that after kill -TERM of the C remote helper, its child (pid 269397) was reparented to init and still held the flock on ttyACM1. The script had to pkill -KILL it.
(3) In n5b, C helper A's websocket stayed up for 56.7 s after Kismet closed its source. The C helper has no ping watchdog; the Python helper gives up after 15 s ('no PING from Kismet for 15 s').

Claims with no saved evidence:
- the n1 strace details (/tmp/hw2/strace now holds only n15's two files)
- the raw.py 'rst:0x15' output and the five bootmode.py attempts
- the 'all four held' --list output
- the n4r 200 -> 400 counts
- the 'no CHANNELS writes over 2 min' strace (glock ran 31 s)

Other weak points:
- The BLE CRC 'ok' result is circular: the firmware computes the CRC itself (firmware/main/esp32c5_sniffer.c ble_adv_crc).
- The capability check proves nothing, because Kismet itself had no capabilities.
- The 1b switch-time categories cannot be told apart.
- 4c passes only with type=.
- Python check 5 cites a log line that does not exist.
- The documented Python exit status 1 cannot be reached.

Key files: C:\Users\oshria\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-oshria-OneDrive-Documents-GitHub-esp32c5-wireshark-sniffer\75fe8a4e-1aa2-48f3-9e8d-8f12a0275438\scratchpad\hw2\results\e2e\hw2 (n1*, n2b, n5b, n8r, n8b, n8t, g3, glock*), ...\hw2\results\hw2 (glock.pcapng, glock2.devs.json, strace\), ...\hw2\py\results\py (p5.hold.log, p6.out, p6b.out, p7-*.log, p21b/c.out).

challenged.claim: C 1a: four local sources at once by the short names; all running=1, 0 error samples (n1c, g4)
challenged.reason: Confirmed: n1c.poll has 600 samples with no error or not-running sample, and 1688/1700/0/1822 packets. The sources were split with hop_offset 21/0. g4 matches. Caveats: running=1/error=0 in REST says little about health. In n1 the hung BTLE source showed running=1, error=0 for its first 15 s (0.9 to 16.1 s) without ever capturing. In n1c the BTLE board also went through 'port closed, reconnecting' (a USB re-enumeration, devnum 13->14) that the metric cannot see. The Zigbee source got 0 packets in both runs, so 802.15.4 reception rests only on its 'capturing' line. Reception on 802.15.4 is shown separately in glock/glock2.

challenged.claim: C 1b: radio-switch time at start, launched -> capturing (1.05/1.50/1.51/1.62/1.49/2.50 s)
challenged.reason: The numbers match the logs, but they measure the helper's fixed handshake, not the radio switch. The helper sends MODE whenever it does not know the board is already on its radio, sends START after MODE_SETTLE_S=0.8 s, and its IPC writes go out about every 0.5 s (g4.s0). A same-radio start took 1.05 s in n1 but 1.50 s in n1c, the same as every switch and every g1a/b/c run, so the data cannot tell switch types apart. The 'Wi-Fi->BTLE 1.50 s (n1b)' figure has no recorded prior radio: there is no n1b.sh or probe output. By the claim itself, the raw open just before n1b (raw.py 07:54:12, n1b 07:54:39) left that board in BLE mode, so n1b may have been BLE->BLE.

challenged.claim: C 1c: Wi-Fi->BTLE switch unreliable; hang intermittent, cause not isolated
challenged.reason: The failure itself is confirmed. n1.log shows 'port closed' at +1.50 s, 'no answer' at +7.62 s, 'IPC connection closed' at +15.23 s, re-open failures at 21/41/64 s, and 145 error samples; the device number went 8->13. Several supporting details have no saved evidence, though. The n1 strace (TIOCNXCL=EIO, openat ENOENT, MODE BLE re-sent at 27.82 s) is gone: /tmp/hw2/strace holds only n15's two files. The raw.py 'rst:0x15' output and the five bootmode.py attempts are saved nowhere in hw2, ~/e2e or /tmp/hw2. The n1b re-run has an unverified prior radio (see 1b). USB re-enumeration on a MODE change is not specific to BLE or to one board: it happened in g4 (C9:10, Zigbee->Wi-Fi) and in n1c. The Python helper did Wi-Fi->BTLE 5/5 on the same board 7D:54 (p12.res). That points at the C helper's reconnect path at least as much as at an intermittent board, which the claim does not weigh.

challenged.claim: C 1d: kismet.datasource.channel stays at the start channel while the helpers hop 5 times a second
challenged.reason: Confirmed. n1c, g4, n8b and n1d polls show a single channel value. There are 50 CHANNELS writes per 10 s in g4.s0/s1, 156 in n8b.strace and 100 in n1d.strace, 200 ms apart. The run misses the cause. Kismet sets this field only from PROBE, OPEN and CONFIGURE reports (kis_datasource.cc lines 1209/1486/1751), so the wiki's premise in question 26 (the C helper 'updates the framework's current channel on every hop') cannot show in REST unless the helper sends a report.

challenged.claim: C 2: --list/--version idle and with boards held, including 'all four held: No supported data sources found..., exit=2'
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n2.out and n2b.out: 12 rows idle, 9 with ttyACM0 held, 6 with ttyACM1 also held, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Output to stderr with exit 2 is stock capture_framework.c behaviour. The 'all four held' result has no saved evidence: that text is not in any hw2 file, ~/e2e or /tmp/hw2.

challenged.claim: C 3: bare names, missing ttyACM9 and bad mode=/channel= are reported and retried every 5.2-6.0 s
challenged.reason: Confirmed in g3.log and g3.src.json: retry_attempts 5, the stated texts, the zero UUIDs and the 'Conflict' lines. Minor points: the first retry gap was 5.09-5.10 s, not 5.2. Kismet also logged duplicate re-open attempts (esp32c5zigbee at 5.62 and 5.63 s, badch200-typed twice at 11.65 s), probably a side effect of the all-zero UUID collision. The run does not report them.

challenged.claim: C 4a: zigbee channel=20,channel_hop=false plus TXTEST 200 gives ch 20, hop 0, 200 packets; n4r re-run 200 -> 400
challenged.reason: The core holds: glock.poll shows ('20',0) in all 152 samples, and glock.pcapng has 200 link-type-230 records with fc 0x8841, pan 0x1234. The details are loose. 'No other CHANNELS writes over 2 min' has no saved strace, and glock ran only 31 s; the 2-minute run was glock2. The device records (tx 200, rx 200, +9 dBm) come from glock2.devs.json, not glock. n4r has no saved output, so the 200 -> 400 counts cannot be checked. n4r ran the Python and C sessions one after the other on the same UUID, so the C session's REST hop=0 is confounded by Kismet keeping per-UUID options (Python finding 1); only its strace, 'MODE 802154' then 'CHANNELS 20\nSTART', stands on its own. There was no negative control (a frame sent on another channel). The RSSI was +9 dBm on every frame (min = max = 9), which looks like saturation or an offset and was not questioned.

challenged.claim: C 4b: Wi-Fi channel=36,channel_hop=false puts every packet on 5180 MHz
challenged.reason: Confirmed. pcapng.py on glock.pcapng gives 4813/4813 frames at freq=5180. The firmware takes the frequency from each packet's rx_ctrl->channel, so this is real per-packet evidence. REST shows ('36',0) in every sample.

challenged.claim: C 4c: invalid channel= refused with a clear reason
challenged.reason: The reason is clear only with type=esp32c5. The usual form, -c esp32c5-ttyACM1:channel=15, gets Kismet's misleading 'Unable to find driver ... make sure that any required plugins are loaded', and the source is neither created nor retried (g3.log at 0.94-1.06 s). For the normal command line this check does not pass.

challenged.claim: C 5a: port lock refuses os.open, pyserial and esptool; capture undisturbed; a second C source for another radio is refused
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n2b.out lines 59-77 and 111-123: EBUSY everywhere, esptool exit 2, packets 105 -> 156 with run=1. g1a shows the esp32c5btle-ttyACM0 retries at 208, 213, 219 and 224 s.

challenged.claim: C 5b: a remote helper for a board a running source holds is not refused and takes it over
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n2b.log and n2b.py0.log (the 'running instance will be closed' line), g1a at 132.70 s, and n5b. The claim is broader than the evidence. The takeover happens only when the remote source has the same UUID (same board and same radio). A remote helper for a different radio is refused with 'already in use' (g1a at 177.79 s; Python p5 check 8). This is a direct consequence of 8b's equal UUIDs. n5b also shows that helper A's websocket stayed open for 56.7 s after Kismet closed its source (the lws untag came only when A was killed): the C helper has no ping watchdog.

challenged.claim: C 5c: after close_source the port opens normally
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n5b.out (a): no flock after close, and all three openers returned OPENED.

challenged.claim: C 6: helper runs with no capabilities and NoNewPrivs 1
challenged.reason: Kismet itself ran with CapPrm = CapEff = 0 (n2b.out lines 19-25), so the helper had no capabilities to drop. The zero values say nothing about whether cap_set_proc works. The only effect the helper can be shown to cause is NoNewPrivs 1. The case that matters, a root or setuid launch, was not tested.

challenged.claim: C 7a: SIGKILL of the local helper is recovered in about 6.1 s with the same UUID
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n7.log and gcrash.log. Re-open at +5.06/+5.10/+5.04/+5.55 s, capturing at +6.08/+6.12/+6.06/+6.58 s, first packet at +6.12/+6.18/+6.15 s.

challenged.claim: C 7b: a set_channel lock does not survive a local re-open (source sits on ch 6 with hop 0)
challenged.reason: Confirmed. n7.poll has 645 samples of ('6',0), and each of n7.strace.1-3 shows one 'CHANNELS 6\nSTART' and no hops. gcrash matches.

challenged.claim: C 8a: remote login from KISMET_CAP_USER/PASSWORD only, and from KISMET_CAP_APIKEY, with no secret on the command line
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n8t.out: 5+5 sessions captured and secret_in_cmdline was false. The key had the datasource role and expiration 0. A negative control for the C helper exists in the Python run's p15, where the C login failed.

challenged.claim: C 8b: the remote UUID equals the local one for each board and radio
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n1c, n8t, n1d, n9 and g1a. The trade-off is not stated: the equal UUIDs are exactly what lets a remote helper evict a running local source (5b).

challenged.claim: C 8c: C websocket start-up takes about 5 s and delivers in 5 s bursts
challenged.reason: Confirmed in n8t.out (medians 5.17/5.09 s against 1.00 s for --tcp and 0.99 s for Python). In n8b the REST steps come at 5.2, 10.2, ... s and sendto calls fall only in seconds 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 29-30. The start-up delay and the bursts are one symptom, not two: the strace shows MODE at 0.04 s and START at 0.84 s, so the board was capturing within 1 s and only delivery waited. The likely cause is upstream: in capture_framework.c, cf_commit_ws_packet calls lws_callback_on_writable from the capture thread without lws_cancel_service. The run did not isolate this with a stock helper as a control.

challenged.claim: C 8d: C remote helper reconnects after a Kismet restart and after close_source (pass)
challenged.reason: The reconnects did happen (n8r.out t+3 running, t+6 packets, back 5 s after close_source). The same output shows a defect the run did not report: after 'kill -TERM $A', the helper's child (pid 269397) had ppid 1 and still held the flock on /dev/ttyACM1 2 s later, and needed pkill -KILL. Scoring a reconnect after close_source as a pass also means close_source cannot stop a remote capture. The Python run lists the same behaviour as a problem (its finding 3), so the two runs judge it inconsistently.

challenged.claim: C: the helper's 15 s give-up reason does not reach Kismet (fail)
challenged.reason: Kismet logged only 'IPC connection closed' at +15.07 s (n15.log). The claim should add that the helper did send the reason. strace esp32c5.283245 shows the write to IPC fd 13 at 08:12:37.4009 ('silent: no capture from the board on /dev/pts/1 for 15 seconds; ...') and exit_group 0.45 ms later. So the text is lost on Kismet's side or by the helper exiting right after sending it.

challenged.claim: Python 1: --list output; Python lists held boards, C hides them
challenged.reason: Confirmed in p1.out. The statement that Python --list 'opens no port and does not read /proc/locks' comes from reading the code; nothing traced it.

challenged.claim: Python 2: several sources in one process; identity equals the C helper's
challenged.reason: Confirmed in p2.out and n9.out: the UUIDs and hardware strings match, only capture_interface differs, and opened -> capturing took 0.88-0.95 s.

challenged.claim: Python 3: zigbee channel=20 lock with TXTEST 200 twice; the second 200 are Kismet duplicates
challenged.reason: The lock is confirmed: one MODE and one CHANNELS 20 write, 400 pcapng records, REST ('20',0). Weak points: 'Kismet counts them as duplicates' is an inference nobody checked. kismetdb logged frequency 0.0 for all 400 packets, which the claim does not mention. The +6/+7 dBm RSSI was not validated. There was no negative control.

challenged.claim: Python 4: the port lock holds, but a same-UUID helper knocks the holder off (partial fail)
challenged.reason: Confirmed in p5.out: every opener got EBUSY, add_source returned HTTP 500, the helper for the other radio was refused every 5 s, and the same-UUID helper evicted the holder at 488 packets.

challenged.claim: Python 5: reconnect with the same UUID after a Kismet restart ('Matching new remote source ... reconnected' on SIGTERM restarts)
challenged.reason: The timings and the same UUID are confirmed in p7.out. The quoted log line is wrong: 'Matching new remote source' appears 0 times in all 13 p7-*.log files, and every restart logs 'New remote source ... connected', as expected from a fresh Kismet process.

challenged.claim: Python 6: clean stops exit 0 quickly and release the ports; exit status when no board can be opened
challenged.reason: Confirmed in p5.out: SIGINT 0.505 s, SIGTERM 0.36 s, flocks 2 -> 0. The help epilog of the tested remote.py documents exit status 1 for 'every source ended by itself', and the run shows that path cannot be reached. That mismatch between help and code should have been reported as a finding, not folded into a pass.

challenged.claim: Python 7: logins from the environment, API key and --user combinations; each case captured unless noted
challenged.reason: The end results are backed by p6b.out, which re-ran envkey, adminkey and tcp_args. But p6 itself was contaminated. p5 never stopped its holder helper (pid 327923; p5.hold.log). It kept reconnecting into p6's Kismet with the same login and UUID and captured ttyACM0 at 09:48:51-09:49:06, 09:49:16-37 and 09:49:47-59. That caused p6's 'already in use' refusals (envkey, envkey_and_userpw, adminkey, login_and_key, tcp_args) and the 'Incoming remote connection ... still running' lines in p6.log. The run did not report this.

challenged.claim: Python 8: a port held by the C helper gives one Kismet message set per 5 s reconnect
challenged.reason: Confirmed: 21 lines in 32 s from p5.log, 3 per cycle, cycles about 5.05 s apart.

challenged.claim: Python 9: BLE frames have CRC ok 471/471 and flags 0x0c13; devices on channel 37 / 2402 MHz; 802.15.4 at +6 dBm
challenged.reason: The CRC and its flags are circular. The controller never hands over the received CRC, so the firmware computes it and sets 'CRC checked' and 'CRC valid' on every packet (esp32c5_sniffer.c ble_adv_crc and lines 602-625). 471/471 only shows that two CRC implementations agree; it says nothing about reception. The channel 37 / 2402000 value is a fixed label while the controller scans 37/38/39, so it is wrong for packets heard on 38 or 39. Only ADV_IND and ADV_NONCONN_IND were seen, as expected from rebuilt HCI reports. The positive 802.15.4 RSSI was not validated.

challenged.claim: Python finding 6: minicom takes no lock, so both helpers open a board minicom holds and capture fails
challenged.reason: Supported by p21c.out: the Python helper opened with pyserial's 'returned no data' error, and its packet count stayed at 91, carried over from the earlier session with the same UUID. The C local source opened with 0 packets. p21b's opposite result ('already in use' with minicom holding) was contaminated by leftover screen processes, as p21c's header says.

challenged.claim: Python end state: all four boards in Wi-Fi mode with this project's firmware, nothing running
challenged.reason: 'Nothing running' is confirmed now: no processes, flocks or open fds on ttyACM0-3, and no user units. 'This project's firmware' rests on START answering with link type 127, which other firmware can also do. Board 38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C was reflashed several times that day (1.2.0, back, 1.1.0, 1.0.0, back). The flash-back command and file are not recorded; only the size, 1148592 bytes, matches the merged image. Wi-Fi mode cannot be re-checked without opening the ports.
